rules: Import one form's prelude at a mount site (`ruststream_fred::stream::prelude::*`, `list::prelude` or `pubsub::prelude`), `ruststream_fred::prelude::*` where a file mixes forms, and `ruststream::prelude::*` in a handler file.

Name the descriptor in `#[subscriber(..)]`: `RedisStream` for a consumer group, `RedisList` for a work queue, `RedisPubSub` for a channel, `RedisPubSubPattern` for a glob; a bare `#[subscriber("key")]` needs `RedisBroker::default_group`.

Pick the stream read mode by constructor: `RedisStream::claiming` on Redis 8.4 and later, else `RedisStream::new` with a `RedisStream::reclaim` subscription beside it on the same group; set `min_idle` above the longest handler runtime.
Chain this crate's `.block(d)` after the framework's `.batch(n)` at the mount site; every other read setting belongs on the descriptor, and every publish setting on the policy.

Name the publish policy at the mount site (`.out_reply(Publish)`, `.out(marker, Publish).build()`, `.out_retry(Publish)`); `RedisPublish` is a unit value, `RedisPubSubPublish` and `RedisListPublish` are built with `::new()` or `::default()`.

Key a message with the `.partition_key(k)` step on the publish builder, bounding the slot `Out<impl Publisher<Options = RedisPublishOptions>, Marker>`; `workers(n, by_key)` keeps the order of a key on the consuming side.

Cap redeliveries with `.max_attempts(n).dead_letter(name)` after `include`; a `RedisPubSubPattern` registration also names where a retry copy goes with `.out_retry(policy).to(name)`, or it does not start.

Serve `retry_after` with the runtime's copy by default, with `RedisStream::delayed_retry(DelayedRetry::DurableZset { .. })` when the delay must survive a restart, or with `claiming` when rounding up to `min_idle` is acceptable.

Use transactions on a stream publisher on standalone or sentinel: `.out_reply(TransactionalPublish).transactional()` for a batch's replies, `publisher.transaction()` for a buffer of its own; a cluster refuses both at startup.

Open a consumer window with `b.include(handler.pipeline())`, `.atomic()` for one `MULTI` / `EXEC` per delivery; queue Redis commands through `Ctx<keys::Pipeline>`, and take `Ctx<keys::FredPool>` for an answer needed now.
Put a pipelined handler's publishes in its round: the reply with `.out_reply(Publish).transform(InRound)`, a slot bounded `Out<impl Bindable>` with `pipeline.bind(out)`.

On a cluster write a reliable list's key under a hash tag, `RedisList::new("{jobs}")`, so the default processing list shares its slot; a subscription whose two keys land on different slots does not start.

Name the envelope, how headers travel beside the payload, once on the broker with `RedisBroker::envelope(FastStream)` (or `NoOp`, `Framed::new(codec)`); a subscription overrides it at the mount site, `b.include(handler.envelope(NoOp))` (the manual path on the descriptor, `RedisList::new(key).envelope(NoOp)`), and a publish policy with `.envelope(..)`.

Test by handing `ruststream::testing::TestApp::start` the service's own app and addressing `tb.broker::<RedisBroker>()`; run the same body against a server with `TestApp::start_live` for scripts, failover, authentication and TLS.
